name: Capri Holdings Limited
reason: Fading fashion brands with adjusted EPS of USD 1.50 in FY2025 vs 6.21 in FY2021 (0.24x the 10y max), EBIT margin down from 24.9% to 2.4%, and net debt/EBITDA 6.3x, so this is a turnaround, not a durable franchise.

name: IHS Holding Ltd.
reason: Nigeria-centred tower company with GAAP losses in every year 2018-24 (EPS -5.93 in 2023), 10y avg ROIC -15.9%, net debt/EBITDA 4.1x and naira devaluation repeatedly wiping out USD-reported earnings.

name: Modern Times Group MTG AB
reason: Hit-driven mobile games roll-up whose EPS growth comes from acquisitions (acquisitions 2.84x 10y FCF, shares +4.5%/yr), with adjusted EPS of SEK 10.17 far above GAAP (297% average gap) and 10y avg ROIC of 2.2%.

name: Inchcape plc
reason: Auto distributor with a thin 5.9% EBIT margin at the 91st pctile of its history, net debt/EBITDA 3.5x and only 4.5%/yr 10y EPS CAGR (GBP 0.52 to 0.80); its earnings depend on OEM contracts and the car cycle, with no specialness.

name: Drax Group plc
reason: Biomass generator whose GBP 1.34 adjusted EPS (up from 0.01 in 2017) depends on UK subsidies that step down after 2027; consensus is -38.9% for FY1 and -33.6% for FY2, a regulatory cliff.

name: HORNBACH Holding AG & Co. KGaA
reason: DIY retailer with a 3.9% EBIT margin, 10y avg ROIC of 4.8%, EUR EPS of 8.81 still below the 12.63 peak in FY2021, and a 4.2% LTG consensus; cheap but ordinary.

name: Ratos AB
reason: Swedish holding company of mid-cap industrials and construction businesses with 10y avg ROIC of 1.4%, adjusted EPS of SEK 2.16 vs 4.12 in 2015 (10y CAGR -6.3%), and a record of portfolio churn.

name: FDJ United
reason: France's lottery monopoly (to 2044) earns a 21.6% avg ROIC and EUR EPS rose from 0.70 in 2019 to 2.63, but the state holds about 21% and raised gaming taxes in 2025 (FY1 consensus -14.3%), and the Kindred deal makes future growth partly acquired and online-betting cyclical.

name: RHI Magnesita NV
reason: Refractories supplier tied to steel volumes, with EUR adjusted EPS of 1.55 in 2025 vs 4.90 in 2019 (0.32x the 10y max), 5y EPS CAGR -11.3%, acquisitions 0.81x 10y FCF and net debt/EBITDA 2.95x.

name: Frontline Plc
reason: Crude tanker owner whose earnings follow spot freight rates (EPS -0.05 in 2021, then 2.95 in 2023); consensus swings from +508% for FY1 to -48% for FY2, which is unforecastable commodity-type earnings.

name: BP PLC
reason: Integrated oil major whose earnings are set by oil and gas prices and refining margins (USD adjusted EPS of 1.46 in 2022 vs 0.48 in 2025, 10y avg ROIC 1.3%), with consensus of -32% for FY2 and -25% for FY3.

name: PLUXEE N.V.
reason: Meal-voucher float business with a 27.5% EBIT margin and net cash, but its economics depend on regulated fee caps and voucher rules (Brazil's 2025 PAT fee cap, French meal-voucher reform); consensus is -0.6% for FY1 and +0.9% for FY2, with only four years of standalone history since the 2024 spin.

name: Aptiv PLC
reason: Auto electrical supplier exposed to the light-vehicle production cycle (EPS -60% in 2020) with a large adjusted-vs-GAAP gap (153%); EPS rose to USD 6.62 in 2025 mainly through buybacks, and the pending EDS separation plus a 2.7% LTG consensus make the 7% route unclear.

name: Ipsos SA
reason: Survey research group with steady EUR EPS growth (2.37 to 5.50, 8.8% 10y CAGR) and modest leverage (0.84x), but EPS has been flat since 2023 at 5.5 and generative AI and synthetic panels are a credible threat to labour-based fieldwork billing, the same issue as G, DOX and EPAM in the US run.

name: Enea SA
reason: State-controlled Polish utility with coal generation and mining; adjusted EPS collapsed to PLN 0.09 in 2022 (0.02x the 10y max), with tariffs and dividends set by government policy and consensus of -6% for FY2 and -7% for FY3.

name: Yara International ASA
reason: Nitrogen fertiliser producer whose earnings follow European gas and ammonia prices (USD adjusted EPS of 10.98 in 2022 then 1.11 in 2023), with 2.5% 10y EPS CAGR and consensus of -14% for FY2 and -11% for FY3.

name: Saipem S.p.A.
reason: Oil and gas E&C contractor with a history of project write-offs (EBIT margin -31.7% in 2021), recapitalisations (shares +32%/yr over 10y) and 10y avg ROIC -10.6%; earnings depend on the energy capex cycle.

name: Metrovacesa SA
reason: Spanish residential land developer with losses in 6 of 9 years, a 23x NTM P/E and earnings set by the housing and credit cycle; its EBIT margin is at its 10y high (11.4%, 100th pctile).

name: HORNBACH Baumarkt AG
reason: Operating subsidiary of HBH (thinly traded after the 2022 squeeze-out) with a 3.6% EBIT margin and 10y avg ROIC of 3.8%; it is the same ordinary DIY economics as HBH-DE and has no adjusted EPS after 2020.

name: PDD Holdings Inc.
reason: Exceptional growth (RMB EPS from 9.56 in 2021 to 82.71 in 2024) and net cash, but EPS fell 12.5% in 2025, Temu faces US/EU tariff and de minimis rule changes, and the Cayman/VIE structure under PRC oversight makes 5-10y earnings unforecastable.
